blurb:
If you're heading to The Battery this Saturday, Dueling Pianos at Park Bench is worth building your night around.

The show runs from 8:30 to 11:30 PM. No cover charge, but seating fills up fast and general seating is first come, first served, so if you've got a group, reserving a table ahead of time is the right call. Dueling Pianos is one of those formats that sounds corny until you're actually in the room and the whole crowd is singing along to something you didn't expect. It's interactive, it's loud, and it's a genuinely fun night out for a group that wants something with more energy than a typical dinner.

The Battery is about 20 minutes from East Cobb and easy to park once you're there. No cover makes this a low-commitment, high-upside Saturday night.
scoring_notes: Good fit for couples and groups within the 40s demographic. No cover lowers the barrier. The Battery is a familiar destination for East Cobb residents. The main drawback is that Dueling Pianos runs regularly at Park Bench, which reduces uniqueness. Included because the November 14 date is confirmed in-window and the audience match is strong.

event_name: Before, At, and Beyond 250: Indigenous Cultural History in Georgia
time: Check Marietta History Center for session times
blurb:
The Marietta History Center is hosting a public symposium this Friday called Before, At, and Beyond 250, focused on indigenous cultural history in Georgia, timed around the country's 250th anniversary.

This is not a lecture series you'll find every weekend. It's a focused academic symposium at a local history institution, which means the content is going to be substantive and the people in the room are going to be genuinely interested. For East Cobb readers who care about the region's deeper history (and a lot of them do), this is the kind of event that's easy to skip because it doesn't have flashing lights attached to it. That would be a mistake.

Check the Marietta History Center for exact session times and registration details. These kinds of events fill up with people who actually show up, so don't wait until Friday morning to look into it.
scoring_notes: High education rate in East Cobb (65% bachelor's or higher) makes a history symposium a genuine fit. One-time event with real academic credibility. Skews slightly older and more intellectually oriented, which aligns with the established family and empty nester segments. Limited details are a drawback but the event itself is clearly legitimate.

event_name: KSU Symphony Orchestra: America at 250, Vol. 3
blurb:
The KSU Symphony Orchestra closes out the week Wednesday evening with the third installment of their America at 250 series, a season built around celebrating the 250th anniversary of the United States through the work of American composers.

This performance features a world premiere of sorts: Inter Alia, a song cycle for soprano and orchestra written by new faculty composer David Kirkland Garner, with BSOM faculty artist Samantha Frischling as the featured soloist. That's not a standard program. You're getting new music, performed by the people who made it, at a concert hall less than 20 minutes from most of East Cobb.

If you haven't been to Morgan Concert Hall, it's a genuinely impressive venue for a weeknight out. The symphony sounds great in that room. And if you're the kind of person who wants to see something actually meaningful before the holiday chaos fully sets in, this is a solid call.
scoring_notes: High education level in East Cobb makes this a reasonable fit. World premiere of a new composition adds real uniqueness beyond a typical orchestra performance. KSU is local and familiar. The evening time on a Wednesday limits casual attendance but suits the established, culturally engaged segment of the audience.

event_name: Glover Park Brewery Chili Cook Off
time: Check Glover Park Brewery for details
blurb:
Nothing says mid-November like a chili cook off, and Glover Park Brewery is hosting one this Sunday.

Glover Park sits right on Atlanta Street in Marietta, a short drive from most of East Cobb. A chili competition at a brewery is exactly what it sounds like: good food, cold beer, and the kind of casual Sunday afternoon that's hard to beat when the weather finally starts feeling like fall. These events tend to draw a good crowd, and the competitive element gives it more energy than a regular Sunday afternoon at a taproom.

Details are still coming in on this one, so check Glover Park's social channels for the full rundown before you head over.
scoring_notes: Casual, locally anchored, and seasonally relevant. Good fit for families with older kids or adult-only pairs. The event-specific nature (cook off vs. just visiting the brewery) gives it enough uniqueness to include. Limited event details are a drawback.

event_name: White Christmas Sing Along at The Strand
price: Check The Strand for ticket prices
blurb:
The Strand is kicking off the holiday film season this Wednesday with a sing-along screening of White Christmas, the 1954 classic with Bing Crosby, Danny Kaye, Rosemary Clooney, and Vera-Ellen.

This isn't just a movie. It's a sing-along, which means the words are on screen and the audience is part of the show. White Christmas is one of those films that people have strong memories attached to, grandparents, holiday traditions, the whole thing. Seeing it at The Strand, a beautiful historic theater right on the Square, makes it feel like an occasion instead of just an afternoon.

The 2:00 PM Wednesday showing works especially well if you've got a flexible schedule or a retiree in the family who's been looking for a reason to get out. Grab tickets early. The Strand doesn't have a lot of seats, and holiday programming fills up.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for the empty nester and established family segments. The Strand is a beloved local venue. Sing-along format makes it a genuine experience, not just a film screening. Wednesday afternoon limits the working-age crowd but suits retirees and flexible schedules well. Good holiday momentum.

blurb:
Contrast Artisan Ales is celebrating their anniversary on Saturday, and they're doing it right.

The party runs from noon to 8:00 PM at their spot on Church Street in Marietta. Live music, merch drops, and commemorative glassware, which means you'll leave with something worth keeping. These are the people making some of the most interesting craft beer in the Marietta area, and an anniversary party at a craft brewery is a different vibe than a typical Saturday bar crawl. It's an event with a reason behind it.

No cover to get in. Show up when you want, stay as long as you want. If you've been meaning to check out Contrast and just haven't made it over yet, this is probably the best possible excuse.
scoring_notes: Anniversary events at local breweries carry a one-time uniqueness that a regular Saturday tap room visit doesn't. Good fit for the adult and empty nester crowd. Free entry lowers the barrier significantly. Locally anchored in Marietta, which is East Cobb's social hub.

blurb:
Thanksgiving is a week out, and Deep Roots Wine Market is making a strong case for how to spend your Sunday evening.

The Perfect Pour is a seasonal tasting featuring four wines built for the holiday table: Iron Horse Wedding Cuvée, Willakenzie Rosé, Willakenzie Estate Pinot Noir, and Botella by Sea Smoke Pinot Noir. Light bites are included. The lineup is legitimately good. Sea Smoke and Willakenzie are not grocery store pours.

It runs from 6:30 to 8:00, which means you're home at a reasonable hour on a Sunday and you've already figured out what you're bringing to Thanksgiving dinner. That's efficient. 107 Church Street in Marietta, right in the Square neighborhood. Grab tickets before they go.
scoring_notes: Perfect fit for the 42-year-old, $118K household audience. These are wine buyers who care about labels and quality. The Thanksgiving timing is a genuinely useful hook. Adult-only skew works well for the empty nester portion of the audience. Highly local, easy to attend.

event_name: Holiday Cookie Crawl on Marietta Square
time: Evening (check Marietta Square for exact hours)
blurb:
The holidays are officially starting on Marietta Square this Friday, and this is the event that kicks it all off.

The Holiday Cookie Crawl, presented by the Georgia Symphony Orchestra, runs alongside Candlelight Shopping, the traditional start to the holiday season on the Square. You get a collectible bag and a passport, then work your way through 12 local businesses collecting 12 different cookies from local bakeries along the way. It's part scavenger hunt, part holiday stroll, part excuse to drag the whole family out of the house before the season really gets going.

The Square is going to be lit up, the shops are open, and there's plenty of room to grab dinner or drinks in between stops. This is the kind of evening that actually feels like the holidays, not just another errand run. If you've been waiting for the season to start, this is your sign.
scoring_notes: Marietta Square is East Cobb's backyard. This is a family-friendly event that also works for couples and empty nesters. It's the official holiday kickoff for the area, which makes it genuinely can't-miss for the week. High demographic fit across the board.
